```{python}
#| output: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_line, geom_histogram, geom_abline,
    labs, theme_minimal,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "mlb" / "hitting_models" / "parquet").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
HM = ROOT / "mlb" / "hitting_models" / "parquet"

def fam(stem):
    fs = sorted(HM.glob(f"{stem}_*.parquet"))
    frames = []
    for f in fs:
        d = pl.read_parquet(f)
        if "season" not in d.columns:
            d = d.with_columns(pl.lit(int(f.stem.rsplit("_", 1)[-1])).alias("season"))
        frames.append(d)
    return pl.concat(frames, how="diagonal_relaxed")

xs = fam("mlb_expected_stats")
xhr = fam("mlb_expected_hr")
proj = fam("mlb_batter_projection")
SEASONS = sorted(xs["season"].unique().to_list())

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))

def mlbam_names(ids):
    """Batched statsapi people lookup; graceful offline fallback to ids."""
    ids = [int(i) for i in ids]
    try:
        import requests
        out = {}
        for i in range(0, len(ids), 80):
            chunk = ids[i:i + 80]
            r = requests.get(
                "https://statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1/people",
                params={"personIds": ",".join(map(str, chunk))}, timeout=20)
            for p in r.json().get("people", []):
                out[int(p["id"])] = p.get("fullName", str(p["id"]))
        return {i: out.get(i, str(i)) for i in ids}
    except Exception:
        return {i: str(i) for i in ids}
```

Three surfaces ship on the `mlb_hitting_models` release tag: **expected
stats** (xwOBA / xBA / xSLG from Statcast contact quality), **expected home
runs** (neutral and park-adjusted xHR from launch conditions), and a
**batter projection** whose fit for season S trains only on seasons < S —
the as-of discipline is enforced by construction, so the projection can be
forward-validated honestly, which this document does below.

The modeling idea is the standard one stated plainly: replace outcome with
contact quality. A batter controls exit velocity, launch angle and spray
far more than they control where fielders stand or which park they hit in,
so expected stats strip defense, park and sequencing luck out of the
batter's ledger. The builders live in sdv-py (`mlb_expected_stats`,
`mlb_expected_home_runs`, `mlb_batter_projection`) over Baseball Savant
batted-ball data; this repository commits the per-season outputs under
`mlb/hitting_models/` and publishes them daily in-season. Everything below
is computed at render time from those committed files.

## Training data

```{python}
tbl = (
    xs.group_by("season").agg(pl.len().alias("batters_xstats"),
                              pl.col("pa").sum().alias("total_pa"))
    .join(xhr.group_by("season").agg(pl.len().alias("batters_xhr")), on="season", how="full", coalesce=True)
    .join(proj.group_by("season").agg(pl.len().alias("batters_projected")), on="season", how="full", coalesce=True)
    .sort("season")
)
gt_show(
    GT(tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Committed hitting-model assets, by season",
                subtitle="from mlb/hitting_models/parquet/; computed at render time")
    .fmt_number(columns=["total_pa"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
)
```

## Known anomalies, reproduced live

**Scale drift in the published xwOBA.** League-mean xwOBA should sit near
.320 in every season; the committed assets do not. This table recomputes the
per-season mean on every render and flags seasons outside a generous
.280–.360 band — several seasons fail, which corrupts every cross-column and
cross-season comparison below and is the leading suspect for the other two
flags in this document:

```{python}
scale = (
    xs.filter(pl.col("pa") >= 100).group_by("season")
    .agg(pl.col("xwoba").mean().alias("mean_xwoba"),
         pl.col("xba").mean().alias("mean_xba"), pl.len().alias("n"))
    .with_columns(((pl.col("mean_xwoba") < 0.28) | (pl.col("mean_xwoba") > 0.36))
                  .alias("OUT_OF_BAND"))
    .sort("season")
)
gt_show(
    GT(scale.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="FLAGGED: league-mean xwOBA by season vs plausible band (.280–.360)",
                subtitle="means of .44–.73 are impossible on the wOBA scale — the builder mis-scales some seasons")
    .fmt_number(columns=["mean_xwoba", "mean_xba"], decimals=3)
)
```

The 2026-09-01 audit flagged that **xwOBA and xBA correlate negatively** on
the published asset — two expected-stat columns that should agree in sign.
This document recomputes that correlation on every render so the anomaly
stays visible until the builder is fixed, rather than being quietly
forgotten:

```{python}
anom = (
    xs.filter(pl.col("pa") >= 100)
    .group_by("season")
    .agg(pl.corr("xwoba", "xba").alias("pearson_xwoba_xba"), pl.len().alias("n"))
    .sort("season")
)
gt_show(
    GT(anom.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="FLAGGED: Pearson r between xwOBA and xBA (PA ≥ 100), by season",
                subtitle="expected-stat columns should correlate strongly positive; investigate builder scaling/join before trusting cross-column comparisons")
    .fmt_number(columns="pearson_xwoba_xba", decimals=3)
)
```

## Expected home runs

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Observed HR vs park-adjusted xHR — the diagonal is neutral luck."
xh = xhr.filter(pl.col("season") == latest)
(
    ggplot(xh.to_pandas(), aes("xhr_park_adj", "hr"))
    + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + geom_point(alpha=0.4, color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="park-adjusted xHR", y="observed HR", title=f"HR vs xHR — {latest}")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
top = xh.sort("hr_above_expected", descending=True).head(10)
names = mlbam_names(top["batter"].to_list())
top = top.with_columns(
    pl.col("batter").map_elements(lambda i: names[int(i)], return_dtype=pl.Utf8).alias("player"),
    ("<img src='https://img.mlbstatic.com/mlb-photos/image/upload/w_120,q_100/v1/people/"
     + pl.col("batter").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8) + "/headshot/67/current' height='42'/>").alias("headshot"),
)
gt_show(
    GT(top.select("headshot", "player", "hr", "xhr_neutral", "xhr_park_adj", "hr_above_expected").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Largest HR over-performers vs xHR — {latest}",
                subtitle="hr_above_expected = observed HR − park-adjusted xHR")
    .fmt_markdown(columns="headshot")
    .fmt_number(columns=["xhr_neutral", "xhr_park_adj", "hr_above_expected"], decimals=1)
    .cols_label(headshot="", player="Player", hr="HR", xhr_neutral="xHR (neutral)",
                xhr_park_adj="xHR (park)", hr_above_expected="HR − xHR")
)
```

## Evaluation — forward validation of the batter projection

Because the projection for season S trains only on seasons < S, joining each
projection to the *realized* xwOBA of the same batter in season S is a true
out-of-sample test. Computed across every committed pair of adjacent
seasons:

```{python}
real = xs.filter(pl.col("pa") >= 100).select("batter", "season", "xwoba")
pj = proj.select("batter", "season", "proj_xwoba", "proj_pa")
fwd = pj.join(real, on=["batter", "season"], how="inner")
by_season = (
    fwd.group_by("season")
    .agg(pl.corr("proj_xwoba", "xwoba").alias("pearson"),
         (pl.col("proj_xwoba") - pl.col("xwoba")).abs().mean().alias("MAE"),
         pl.len().alias("batters"))
    .sort("season")
)
pooled = fwd.select(
    pl.corr("proj_xwoba", "xwoba").alias("pearson"),
    (pl.col("proj_xwoba") - pl.col("xwoba")).abs().mean().alias("MAE"),
    pl.len().alias("batters"),
).with_columns(pl.lit("pooled").alias("season")).select("season", "pearson", "MAE", "batters")
out = pl.concat([by_season.with_columns(pl.col("season").cast(pl.Utf8)), pooled])
gt_show(
    GT(out.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Projection forward validation — proj_xwoba vs realized xwOBA (PA ≥ 100)",
                subtitle="the projection for season S trained only on < S; this join is out-of-sample by construction")
    .fmt_number(columns=["pearson", "MAE"], decimals=3)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Projected vs realized xwOBA, all forward-validated seasons pooled."
(
    ggplot(fwd.to_pandas(), aes("proj_xwoba", "xwoba"))
    + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + geom_point(alpha=0.2, color="#2a6f97", size=0.8)
    + labs(x="projected xwOBA (as-of)", y="realized xwOBA",
           title="Batter projection — out-of-sample")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

A sane aging-curve projection lands in the 0.5–0.7 correlation range with
next-season xwOBA; the observed values in the table above are **far below
that**, hovering near zero. Given the scale-drift flag reproduced earlier —
realized league-mean "xwOBA" of .44–.73 in several seasons — the honest
reading is that the *published expected-stats columns are corrupted*, not
that the projection carries no signal: a forward validation against a
mis-scaled target cannot exonerate or condemn the model. The builder fix
comes first; this table then becomes the projection's real gate. The publish
gates additionally anchor the expected stats themselves: xwOBA/xBA Spearman
vs Savant's own published expected stats ≥ 0.95 on identical inputs, and xHR
full-season Spearman vs live ≥ 0.90 — gates that plainly did not catch the
scale drift, which is itself a finding about the gates.

## Provenance & reproducibility

- **Trained on:** Baseball Savant batted-ball data (exit velocity, launch
  angle, spray), seasons in the table above; the projection for season S
  uses seasons < S only.
- **Committed at:** `mlb/hitting_models/parquet/`; published to
  `mlb_hitting_models`; per-publish metadata in
  [`../../mlb/hitting_models/mlb_hitting_models_card.json`](../../mlb/hitting_models/mlb_hitting_models_card.json).
- **Pipeline:** `scripts/mlb_models.sh 02` → stage
  `python/mlb_model_02_hitting.py` (`mlb_models_cron.yml`). Single home:
  `models/manifest.yaml`.
- **Rebuild this document:** `scripts/render_model_docs.sh` (Quarto → GFM;
  `uv sync --group docs`). Player names/headshots resolve via one batched
  statsapi call; offline renders fall back to MLBAM ids.

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Publish observed stats alongside** — the asset carries expected stats
  only; adding observed wOBA/BA would make luck-vs-skill deltas a one-liner
  for consumers (today it needs a second source).
- **Known issue:** the projection's validated window starts at 2018; earlier
  seasons ship but sit outside the gates.
- **FLAGGED ANOMALY (2026-09-01, reproduced live above):** xwOBA vs xBA on
  the published assets correlates NEGATIVELY — expected-stat columns should
  agree in sign; investigate column scaling / join keys in the builder
  before trusting cross-column comparisons. This document recomputes the
  correlation on every render so the flag cannot silently go stale.
- **FLAGGED ANOMALY (2026-09-01, reproduced live above):** league-mean
  "xwOBA" of .44–.73 in several published seasons is impossible on the wOBA
  scale — per-season scale drift in the builder is the leading suspect for
  BOTH the negative xwOBA↔xBA correlation and the near-zero projection
  forward validation. The publish gates (Spearman vs Savant on identical
  inputs) are rank-based and therefore scale-blind — add an absolute
  league-mean band gate so this class cannot ship again.
